chapters.title: A protected first period for every new role
chapters.lede: Induction gives each newcomer — a teacher, a principal, a whole school — the right structured support and a protected development period **before** any formal judgement.

blocks.lead: Right role → right document → right support → right stage → **next action**.
points: **Six tracks** — Teacher, Principal, Subject Specialist, School, Academic Coordinator and Exams Officer. Each has its own handbook.
**Induction is not appraisal.** Nothing collected during induction is used for a formal score, KPI or rating. Ever.
**Induction is not probation.** Support runs for the full programme, whatever the contract type.
**The outcome is never a score or a grade** — it is completion, Certified, Ready or Extended.

blocks.title: Induction and appraisal never mix
blocks.text: Mentor observations, developmental placements, journal entries, weekly pulses and private mentoring notes **never** enter appraisal. After induction, appraisal starts with **fresh evidence**. Only the completion status and teacher-approved PD priorities move forward.

source.at: §13 Keep Induction and Teacher Appraisal Separate

blocks.title: Safeguarding is the one exception
blocks.text: Induction conversations stay private — except a **child-protection concern**, which is always reported **immediately** to the Designated Safeguarding Lead, in every track. Never investigate it yourself, and never put safeguarding details in the induction tracker.

chapters.title: Running Teacher Induction in your school
chapters.lede: You do not need to mentor every new teacher or read every mentoring note. You make sure the system works. Start with the Oversight Guide and the Induction Control Centre.

blocks.text: “Is every induction teacher receiving the **correct support**, from the **correct person**, at the **correct stage**?” Track the process — not private mentoring conversations.

blocks.title: Common questions

items.q: Does induction affect anyone's appraisal score?
items.a: No, in any track. Induction-period data never feeds a formal appraisal score, KPI or rating. The appraisal cycle begins only after induction is complete, with fresh evidence.

items.q: Is induction the same as probation?
items.a: No. Induction is support, not a trial period. Under Indonesian labour law probation only exists in a permanent contract and is capped at three months; induction support runs for the full programme whatever the contract.

items.q: What if a mentor match is not working?
items.a: Raise it with the mentor first, then the next level in the track's route. Teacher and Principal Induction have a no-fault mentor-change route, with a replacement target within 14 days. Raising a concern never disadvantages the participant.

items.q: Should the Subject Specialist mentor every new teacher in their subject?
items.a: No. A Subject Specialist supports the mentor and teacher when specialist knowledge is needed. Only when formally assigned as a mentor do they follow the Mentor Guide and certification rules.

items.q: Can a large school run induction as group sessions?
items.a: Partly. Common topics can be taught together, but the named mentor, subject-specific discussion, required observations and personal action planning stay individual. A workshop never replaces the mentor.
